long_biography.plain_text:
In 2008, Turki established Rabigh Wings Aviation Academy, an early Saudi flight-training school that later became AeroGuard Arabia. The venture gave institutional form to his interest in flying and pilot education. He subsequently led the Saudi Air Sports Federation and chaired Saudi Development and Training Company. That business delivered training and manpower services to aviation and defence customers.

None of those positions explains how Prince Turki's private capital was formed. He controls more than a quarter of TMA Limited Partnership and holds appointment rights and significant influence. However, its operating sector, assets and value are not publicly disclosed. His title and career therefore cannot determine the industry, origin or ownership relationship behind his principal wealth.

uncertainties.detail: No neutral source identifies the industry, origin or ownership relationship responsible for Prince Turki's principal personal wealth. All four classifications remain Unknown rather than being inferred from royal status, relatives, public roles or state assets.

Companies House establishes significant beneficial control but does not disclose the partnership's operating sector, underlying assets, value or contribution to Prince Turki's finances. The filing is therefore identity and control evidence, not a wealth classification.

The academy founding, air-sports presidency and training-company chairmanship establish a coherent aviation career. The sources do not establish the size, current ownership or personal financial importance of those interests, so aviation is not promoted as a wealth classification.

The source record duplicates the honorific by storing Prince in both title and display_name, and stores the patronymic lineage inside first_name. The proposals retain Prince in title, set first_name to Turki and move bin Muqrin bin Abdulaziz to middle_names.
The existing Wikipedia URL resolves to the correct identity. No dedicated personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website was verified strongly enough to propose.

Politics, controversies, allegations, legal matters, sanctions, private-family trivia and vessel research are excluded. Royal lineage is used only as part of the exact public name and never as evidence of personal wealth.
